fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Nighttime conspicuity of a HAWK display is a recognized, site-specific safety issue affecting drivers' ability to detect and obey the stop display over an active pedestrian crossing, squarely within final-design-stage audit scope.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim (driver confusion from competing night-time background elements) is directly supported by the verbatim quoted recorded input fact EV-US-01 tied to the exact intersection; no invented content detected.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern under FHWA RSA practice with no conflation into MUTCD compliance questions; conspicuity framing respects framework semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reflective border on the HAWK signal is specific, actionable, low-cost, and viable at final design stage, naming the treatment and location rather than a null action.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the exposed road users if drivers miss or misread the display, pairing driver-side conspicuity with VRU protection at the crossing.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance adequacy at HAWK crossings on the corridor's highest pedestrian-collision-frequency sites is a substantive final-design-stage safety issue affecting slow-clearing users exposed to conflicting releases.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-US-016 provides a verbatim quote ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') directly supporting the pivotal claim, exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern about assumed walking-speed verification rather than a MUTCD compliance assertion, keeping the categorical distinction intact under FHWA final-design audit semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific (all six named HAWK sites), actionable (reprogramme clearance timing), and viable pre-construction via revised assumed walking speed; not null.
justifications.vru_coverage: Elderly pedestrians are explicitly named road users and the entire finding centers on vulnerable-user clearance exposure, so VRU impact is fully considered.
